q: Which of the following is the best aid to show a trend in marks over several years?
exp: A line graph shows change over time clearly.

q: Feedback in microteaching can be obtained from:
options: supervisor, peers and video or audio recordings
exp: Multiple sources give objective information about the performance.

q: A unit plan differs from a lesson plan because it:
options: is meant for a single period only
covers a larger part of the syllabus spread over several periods
exp: A unit plan organises a whole unit while a lesson plan covers one period.

q: Correlation among subjects in a curriculum ensures that:
options: the number of subjects is doubled
related ideas in different subjects reinforce one another
exp: Correlation links subjects so that learning is more meaningful.

q: Evaluation is different from measurement because evaluation:
options: includes value judgement about the quantitative and qualitative evidence
exp: Measurement gives numbers; evaluation interprets them against objectives.
sub: Evaluation, formative and summative assessment, CCE

q: An aptitude test is used to:
options: predict future ability to learn or perform in an area
exp: Aptitude tests measure potential.

q: The reliability coefficient normally ranges from:
exp: A value near 1 indicates high reliability.

q: Peer tutoring can help remedial work because:
options: students learn from classmates who explain things in simple language
exp: Peers can provide additional support and explanation.

q: Review of related literature is done to:
options: know what has already been studied and avoid duplication
exp: It identifies gaps and guides the design.

q: A recorded video lecture that a student can watch at any time is an example of:
exp: The learner can access it at a time of choice.

q: SCERT stands for:
options: Standard Council for Education and Research Teaching
School Council of Examination and Reform Training
State Council of Educational Research and Training
State Centre of Educational Records and Testing
exp: SCERT is the state-level academic body for school education.

q: Reflective teaching involves:
options: thinking critically about one's own teaching to improve it
exp: Reflective practice, associated with Schon, uses experience as a basis for improvement.

q: A good way to teach debugging is to:
options: give students programs with errors and ask them to locate and correct them
ask them to memorise error messages
exp: Learning from errors strengthens understanding.

q: Which of the following is an example of intrinsic motivation in a classroom?
options: A student studies to win a cash prize
A student studies to avoid punishment
A student studies to please the examiner
A student solves puzzles because she enjoys the challenge
exp: Intrinsic motivation comes from interest and enjoyment of the activity itself, not external rewards.

q: In the inductive method of teaching:
options: examples are studied first and then a general rule is derived
a rule is stated first and then applied to examples
there is no use of examples
exp: Induction proceeds from particular instances to a general principle.

q: Which of the following is a good practice while using the blackboard?
options: Writing legibly and organising content in a planned layout
Standing in front of the written matter
Writing continuously without erasing or summarising
exp: Legible, planned writing helps all students see and follow the content.

q: The major advantage of microteaching is that it:
options: eliminates the need for school practice
is useful only for experienced teachers
provides a safe, controlled setting for practising and improving specific skills
exp: Its reduced complexity lets trainees master skills before facing real classrooms.

q: The recapitulation questions asked at the end of a lesson serve to:
options: evaluate how far the objectives have been achieved
exp: They check understanding and give feedback.

q: Co-curricular activities such as debates and sports are included in the curriculum to:
options: develop the all-round personality of learners
exp: They support social, emotional and physical development.

q: A student's marks are compared with other students' marks in:
exp: Norm-referenced tests rank students relative to a group.
sub: Evaluation, formative and summative assessment, CCE

q: Anecdotal record is a tool used to:
options: note the significant behaviour incidents of a student
exp: It is a brief factual record of a particular observed event.

q: Cronbach's alpha is used to estimate:
exp: Alpha measures how consistently items measure the same construct.

q: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act came into force in:
exp: The RTE Act was passed in 2009 and came into force on 1 April 2010.

q: A questionnaire is a tool used to:
options: collect information in written form from respondents
exp: It consists of a set of written questions for respondents.

q: PM eVidya was announced to:
options: unify digital, online and on-air education initiatives
exp: It brings together DIKSHA, TV channels, radio and other modes.

q: The National Testing Agency (NTA) is mainly responsible for:
options: conducting entrance examinations for higher education
exp: NTA conducts exams such as JEE Main and NEET.

q: The best way for a teacher to handle misbehaviour is:
options: to understand its cause and respond constructively
to humiliate the student in public
exp: Positive discipline addresses the cause without harming dignity.

q: Parsons problems are exercises in which students:
options: arrange scrambled lines of code in the correct order
exp: They reduce the cognitive load of writing code from scratch.

q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of effective teaching?
options: One-way flow of information with no learner participation
exp: Effective teaching is interactive; one-way talk without participation is not.

q: Which of the following is an essential feature of the project method?
options: It is a purposeful activity carried out in a natural setting
It is done under strict dictation
It avoids the use of real-life problems
exp: Projects are purposeful, problem-oriented and based on real life.

q: While preparing PowerPoint slides for a class, which practice is NOT recommended?
options: Filling each slide with long paragraphs in small font
exp: Overloaded slides reduce attention and are hard to read.

q: Which of the following is NOT a teaching skill in microteaching?
exp: Budget preparation is an administrative task, not a classroom teaching skill.

q: Home assignment in a lesson plan should be:
options: related to the lesson and within the capacity of students
given only to some students as punishment
exp: Meaningful assignments reinforce learning.

q: The principle of flexibility in curriculum means that it should:
options: be adaptable to local needs and changing times
be the same everywhere with no change
exp: A flexible curriculum can be revised and adapted.

q: In criterion-referenced assessment, a student's performance is compared with:
exp: The student is judged on whether the pre-set criterion has been achieved.
sub: Evaluation, formative and summative assessment, CCE

q: A sociometric technique is used to find out:
options: the social relationships and acceptance among students in a group
exp: Sociometry, developed by Moreno, shows preferences and rejections within a group.

q: Inter-rater reliability concerns the:
options: agreement between different scorers marking the same answers
exp: High inter-rater reliability means scorers give similar marks.

q: Differentiated instruction involves:
options: giving the same task to all in the same way
adjusting content, process or product according to learner needs
exp: It accommodates differences in readiness and learning style.
